build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: Each player has a note highway with at least 3 lanes. Notes scroll toward a judgement line and the player hits them with timed key presses. Successful hits charge a power meter displayed prominently. The charge meter fills proportionally to combo length and accuracy. Score 0 if there is no note highway, if hits do not charge a meter, or if there are no lanes.

When the charge meter reaches a threshold, the player can spend it to launch a musical attack (projectile, wave, or blast) that travels across the arena toward the opponent. The opponent takes damage if hit (health bar depletes). Stronger charges (from higher combos) produce visibly more powerful attacks. Score 0 if there is no attack mechanic, if charge cannot be spent, or if attacks have no visual scaling with charge level.

The opponent can dodge or block incoming attacks with a timed key press as the projectile arrives. Successful dodges negate damage with a visual effect. Health bars deplete on successful hits. First player to zero health loses the round. Matches are best-of-3 rounds. Score 0 if there is no dodge mechanic, if health does not deplete, or if there is no round structure.

At least 4 playable characters with distinct visual designs, musical themes, and different special move sets (unique attack types, charge speeds, or passive abilities). Each character has a unique sprite and selection screen preview. Score 0 if there are fewer than 4 characters, if characters look identical, or if they play identically.

At least 3 distinct attack types across characters (e.g., bass wave, treble spike, chord blast) with different visual effects, travel speeds, and damage patterns. Each attack is visually identifiable and has unique properties. Score 0 if there is only one attack type, if attacks all look the same, or if there are fewer than 3 distinct types.

An arcade/ladder mode with at least 5 AI opponents of increasing difficulty. Later opponents have faster note patterns and more aggressive attack usage. Defeating all opponents shows a character-specific victory screen. Score 0 if there is no arcade mode, if there are fewer than 5 opponents, or if difficulty does not escalate.

The tempo increases between rounds in a match, making note patterns denser and combat faster. The player perceives escalating intensity across the best-of-3 structure. Between-round interludes show score and round status. Score 0 if tempo is static, if there is no between-round screen, or if rounds feel identical in intensity.

The split-screen layout is readable: each player's highway, charge meter, and health bar are clearly separated and identifiable. Attack projectiles travel visibly across the arena between the two sides. The player can assess both their own and the opponent's state at a glance. Score 0 if the layout is confusing, if charge meters are hidden, or if attacks are not visible in transit.

Hit feedback on the note highway is immediate and graded (Perfect/Great/Miss with distinct visuals). The charge meter fills with visible animation. Attack launches produce a dramatic visual cue. Dodge successes show a clear evasion effect. Score 0 if there is no hit feedback, if the charge meter jumps without animation, or if attacks launch without visual cue.

The full game loop is connected: Title screen -> Character select -> Fight (note highway + attacks) -> Round results -> Match winner -> Return to menu or next opponent. The player can experience every node without restarting. Score 0 if any transition in the chain is missing or broken.

A title screen is present and styled: it shows the game name in a custom or themed font, has at minimum a play button that is interactive and transitions to character select, and uses a non-default background (neon club, stage lights, or musical arena) — not plain plain grey or a solid-colour fill. Score 0 if the game launches directly into gameplay with no title screen, or if the start button is non-functional. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

Overall art-style coherence: every visible element — character sprites, note gems, attack projectiles, arena background, UI panels — belongs to a single consistent visual language. The palette is vibrant and energetic with a music/club theme; no clashing styles. Score 0 if the screen mixes incompatible styles, or if elements are obviously unthemed placeholder shapes.

Character sprites are detailed and animated, attack projectiles have distinct authored visual effects, the arena background is illustrated with stage/club theming, and UI elements (health bars, charge meters, combo counters) use styled widgets with custom art. Score 0 if characters are solid-colour primitives, if attacks are plain circles, or if UI is unstyled defaults.

Animation continuity and polish: note scrolling, hit bursts, charge meter filling, attack projectile travel, dodge animations, health bar depletion, round transitions, and character select previews each play as smooth multi-frame tweens or sprite animations. No element snaps to its new state in a single frame. Score 0 if any of these moments is instantaneous, or if transitions are hard cuts.
